text: Phishing attacks commonly use urgent or threatening language to pressure victims into clicking a link, opening an attachment, verifying an account, or providing sensitive information.
Credential phishing attempts often imitate trusted login pages or services and ask users to enter usernames, passwords, one-time codes, recovery codes, or other authentication information.
Suspicious URLs may contain misspelled domains, unusual subdomains, misleading paths, excessive URL parameters, shortened links, or domains that do not match the claimed organization.
Phishing messages frequently create artificial urgency by claiming an account will be suspended, a payment will fail, access will expire, or immediate action is required.

Brand impersonation phishing occurs when attackers imitate a legitimate company, bank, government organization, cloud service, social platform, or other trusted entity to make fraudulent communication appear legitimate.

Financial phishing may request payment, banking information, card details, cryptocurrency transfers, invoices, gift cards, or other financial actions while pretending to represent a legitimate organization.
A suspicious message becomes more concerning when multiple indicators appear together, such as an unexpected message, urgent language, a suspicious URL, a credential request, and brand impersonation.
Users should independently visit the official website or contact the organization through a trusted channel instead of using links or contact information provided inside a suspicious message.
